coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Creek Park, east reach
search_aliases: Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge)
record.summary: The stretch of landscaped park -- paths, trees and grass -- between the already-tracked Mission Creek Park Pavilion and the 4th Street bridge, on the south/east (Channel St) bank of Mission Creek; already built, per satellite imagery, and hand-traced from that imagery after an earlier placement transferred from the plan PDF repeatedly mis-located the stretch. OCII's Nov 2024 CAC update map labels this stretch 'Mission Creek Park P1', and the same update's timeline says the first Mission Bay parks opened "at Mission Creek P1" (2002); whether this traced stretch is that P1 is not confirmed, and no source read dates this stretch itself.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- hand-traced from satellite imagery (not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team, and not derived from a placement transferred from the plan PDF, which was unreliable for this specific stretch). Status 'complete' because landscaping (paths, trees and grass) is visible on the strip in USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29) and in the earlier Esri imagery; the cited OCII deck shows 'Mission Creek Park (P3)' as a photo slide with no status text, and no cited source dates or confirms completion of P1.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery), step by step, rather than from a placement transferred from the plan PDF, which repeatedly mis-located this segment.

changes.text: Two records were both titled Mission Creek Park (the second page address ended in -2). The first is the park SF Rec and Park lists as Mission Creek Park (North and South); this one is the stretch between the Mission Creek Park Pavilion and the 4th Street bridge. No source names that stretch separately, so the name is descriptive and the record's open question about which OCII parcel label (P1 or P3) applies is unchanged. Shape, status and use are unchanged; the old page address now redirects to the new one, and the old name still finds the record in search.

changes.text: OCII's timeline gives 2002 for the opening of "Mission Creek P1"; whether this traced stretch is that P1 is not confirmed, and no source read dates this stretch itself. A landscape architect's page describes "Mission Creek Park North" (client Catellus, timeline 1999-2011, built), a project timeline rather than an opening date.

The October 10, 2026 note about this change said the part of the east reach moved to P2 was about 3,800 square metres and that it included about 220 square metres overlapping P2. Measured again from the outlines before and after the change, the east reach lost about 3,740 square metres, and the two shapes had overlapped by about 1,220 square metres. The shape on the map is unchanged.
Added 3 photos taken on site on September 28, 2026.
The east reach of Mission Creek Park now ends at the crosswalk beside the Pavilion.

The record said this park stretch is on Mission Creek's north/west bank; it is on the Channel St (south/east) bank. The map notes said OCII's map did not resolve P1 versus P3; the map's labels put P1 on this stretch and P3 east of 4th St, so the P-number and notes now say P1, and the 'complete' status is attributed to imagery, since the cited deck gives no status. The record's identifier, which still reads P1/P3, has not yet been renamed. The aerial photo credit no longer says it was taken from a departing flight.

open_questions: No source read dates when this specific stretch was built. OCII's Nov 2024 timeline gives 2002 for the opening of "Mission Creek P1", but whether this traced stretch is that P1 is not confirmed. It was hand-traced from satellite imagery because it was visibly already landscaped, not because any source dated its construction.

Pier & Point read OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 as both falling somewhere in this general stretch, based on the Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update' -- but that deck's slide 3 is titled 'MISSION CREEK PARK (P3)', while its slide 2 map image labels 'MISSION CREEK PARK P1' on the south-bank strip and P3 separately; which label (if either) applies to this exact segment, versus to the separately tracked Mission Creek Park record's own P1 (an amphitheater, per OCII's current open-space page), is not resolved.

Name/operator: presumed to be part of the same SF Recreation and Park Department-managed Mission Creek Park system as its neighbors (the department's Mission Creek South list includes "An esplanade (between 3rd and 4th streets)"), but no source read names this specific segment.

As of 2026-09-22, flagged rather than resolved: this record is currently classified 'Mission Bay South' and its own sourcing leans on Mission Bay South's P1/P3 plan labels (see above). But this record's own coordinates sit at the same latitude as other already-tracked Mission Bay North records (The Beacon, Rich Sorro Commons), north of the core of the separately tracked, South-side Mission Creek Park record. A landscape architecture firm's own project page (Munden Fry Landscape Associates, mflastudio.com/mission-creek-park-north) describes "Mission Creek Park North" (client Catellus; "TIMELINE 1999-2011", "STATUS Built", 7.5 acres -- a project timeline, not an opening date) as framed "on the north by mid-rise and tower residential developments and on the south by Mission Creek and a thriving, eclectic house boat community", which matches this record's own traced bank; OCII's September 2023 transition presentation separately lists parcels 'NP1-NP5'. Whether this segment is actually part of Mission Bay North's NP system rather than South's P1/P3 is an open identity question bigger than a date, not resolved here -- flagged for a closer look, possibly including whether this record's site classification itself should change.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the summary previously said this stretch is on Mission Creek's north/west bank; the traced polygon sits on the Channel St side (south/east bank), as does the Pavilion, and OCII's Nov 2024 map shows the P1 label on the south-bank strip. Berry St, the north bank, is about 200 m away.
No source read gives a completion date for this stretch of park (OCII's 2002 date is for "Mission Creek P1", not confirmed to be this reach), and no building-permit search has been made for it.
